opening.headline: When you are confused about whether Gemini is a search, a chatbot, or an assistant, you will learn how to divide the roles of the Gemini app and Live into situations and check the basis and product of the response.
body: When you ask a question like a search box, you get a summarized answer, like a chatbot, it creates drafts and ideas, and when you speak with a voice, it answers verbally like a secretary. Since there are multiple roles under one name, it is difficult to tell what the tool is for.

In this class, we'll first look at what the Gemini app does, Canvas, and activity save settings. Next, we'll look at Live's terms of use for spoken conversations, comparing how to view the relevant sources of responses and tools for verifying AI-generated images, video, and audio. Finally, we explain why voice queries on the move and data creation at the desk use different functions.
objectives: Can explain the role of the Gemini app and Live
Response source verification and product verification functions can be distinguished.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

screens.title: Is it a search, a chatbot, or a secretary?
screens.lead: Let's look at three scenes using Gemini. When you select each item, an explanation will unfold.

items.prompt: Scene 1: Ask a question like a search bar
items.answer: When you enter your question, you will receive a summary of a complex topic in an easy-to-understand manner. Instead of opening the list of search results one by one, you receive a summary first.
Ask them to come up with an idea, create a plan, and create a first draft of an outline, email, or blog post. You can then ask to re-edit the draft you created.
If you speak without typing, Gemini will respond verbally. It is suitable for situations where your hands are not free, such as coming up with ideas while walking or practicing presentations.

Because all three scenes are called by one name: 'Gemini'. It becomes easier to distinguish if you know that the functions used in each scene are different, and the environments and conditions in which they can be used are also different.

screens.outro: First, let me recall my experience communicating with AI using voice.

screens.title: Think back: Have you ever talked to an AI using voice?
screens.lead: Read the questions and think for yourself first. There is no need to submit an answer, and when you select an item, the instructor's thoughts unfold.

items.prompt: Have you ever tried talking to an AI using your voice?
items.answer: The experience of briefly commanding a smartphone assistant is common. In contrast, the way of exchanging long conversations verbally may still be unfamiliar. This class' Live is just that. Even if you've never used it, imagine in what situations you would feel comfortable speaking.

items.prompt: What was different between typing and speaking?
items.answer: Speaking is quick and natural, but it is difficult to change the results by just looking at them. Conversely, typing is slower, but it's good for polishing documents and checking evidence. There are pros and cons depending on the situation.

items.prompt: To what extent do you believe in AI’s answers?
items.answer: It is safe to assume that any answer can be wrong. The topic of this class is whether there is a means to check the evidence and whether there is a way to determine whether the generated image is real.

screens.outro: Now let’s start by looking at what the Gemini app does.

screens.title: What the Gemini App Does
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn about the purpose and terms of use of the Gemini app, Canvas, and activity management.

tabs.label: Use
tabs.body: The Gemini app helps you generate ideas, make plans, and find different ways to get things done. You can also use it to get easy summaries of complex topics or to create outlines, emails, blog posts, or first drafts of poems. On your computer, start a conversation by typing a question or prompt into the input box at the bottom of gemini.google.com.

tabs.label: Terms of Use
tabs.body: You can use some features without signing in, but to use more features or save your activity, you'll need to sign in with your Google Account. You can sign in with a personal Google Account, a work account with a qualifying edition of Workspace (18+), or a school account where your administrator has turned on the service. On your computer, you'll need Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Opera, or Edgium browsers.

tabs.label: Canvas
tabs.body: Create or edit documents, apps, slides, and code with Gemini in Canvas. While logged in, select Canvas from the Add File menu below the input window and enter the prompt. If you need a slide-like format, write it directly in the prompt. Apps and code can be modified through input fields or directly from the Code view, and changes are automatically saved. You can also convert your results into other formats, such as audio outlines or quizzes.

tabs.label: Activities and precautions
tabs.body: Activity in the Gemini app can be viewed and deleted in My Activity, and the Keep Activity setting can be turned off. The Gemini app may make mistakes, so you should double-check your answers and not rely on them for professional advice, such as medical, legal, or financial. Open source licenses may apply when creating and using code, and the user is responsible for its use.

screens.outro: Next, we will take a step-by-step look at Live through verbal communication.

screens.title: Live: Natural conversation using voice
screens.lead: In the next step we will find out what Gemini Live is and under what conditions it can be used. Select the next arrow to proceed.

visual.alt: Scene of verbal conversation by pressing the Live button on the smartphone screen
labels: Help me practice my presentation tomorrow
Okay, start with the first sentence.
Android phone/tablet / Gemini mobile app / Login required

steps.title: What is it?
steps.body: Gemini Live is a feature that allows you to have natural, uninterrupted conversations with Gemini. If you speak without input, Gemini will respond verbally. Just like a human conversation, you can interrupt Gemini to add something or change the subject.

steps.title: what can you do
steps.body: You can use it to brainstorm ideas, plan gift ideas or events, ask about business plans, or explore the details of a topic of interest. It is also suitable for practicing out loud more naturally before an important event.

steps.title: How to get started
steps.body: Open the Gemini mobile app on your Android phone or tablet and tap Live at the bottom or swipe the screen to the left. You can also start with a voice like, “Hey Google, let’s talk live.”

steps.title: Required Conditions
steps.body: You'll need an Android phone or tablet, Gemini set up with the Gemini mobile app or Mobile Assistant, a personal Google account or work or school account with access to the Gemini app, and the latest version of the Google app. You must be logged in to the Gemini app. Live is not available in the Gemini web app.

steps.title: Constraints and Etiquette
steps.body: Gems cannot be used with Live. We also remind you to ask permission and respect someone's privacy before recording them or including them in a Live conversation.

screens.outro: Now that we've established the verbal function, let's look at how to trust the response.

screens.title: View sources and verify products
screens.lead: Switch between the two states to compare the ability to see the source of a response with the ability to verify the product.

states.label: View related sources
states.body: The Gemini app can show sources and related links below the response or in the middle of the text. If there is a Sources button, click it to open related links in the right side panel. The link can be a public website, a file you upload, or a document or email if you're connected to Workspace. Not all responses have a source and if there is no button, no link is provided in the response. If you directly cite a text from a web page in large format, a link to that web page will appear in the source list, and images taken from the web will also show a source link.

states.label: AI product verification
states.body: The Gemini app's verification tool is used to screen images, videos, and audio created or edited by AI and can be used by logged in users. I use two techniques. SynthID is an invisible watermark that Google's AI model determines whether something was created or edited. Content Credentials are like digital passports that record the origin and history of content and are used for both AI and non-AI content. Upload one file at a time, and the size must be less than 100 MB, video must be less than 90 seconds, and audio must be less than 1 hour. For screenshots to be accurate, you must crop the image closely, and do not upload a collage of multiple images.

screens.outro: Now that we've checked the features, let's apply them to two situations.

screens.title: Narrative examples: voice queries on the go and data creation at your desk
screens.lead: The instructor demonstrates the process of choosing different features in two situations. Select the next arrow to follow your decision.

steps.title: Reading the two situations
steps.body: Situation A involves practicing out loud and brainstorming a presentation for your next meeting on the go. Situation B involves writing and editing a draft report at your desk, and even checking the sources. They both use Gemini, but have different features.

steps.title: Step 1: Look at your hand and the situation
steps.body: Situation A is when you are walking or moving, so your hands are not empty and it is easy to talk. In this case, Live is suitable. Open Live in the Gemini mobile app on Android to practice speaking, jumping in and out and developing ideas. I also confirm that you need to log in and that Gems cannot be used together.

steps.title: Step 2: See if the output needs to be changed
steps.body: Situation B requires multiple revisions to the output. In this case, it is best to open Canvas on your computer and create and edit documents with Gemini. If you need a slide-like format, write it directly in the prompt and refine the document that is automatically saved.

steps.title: Step 3: See if the facts matter
steps.body: The report contains facts, so you need to check the basis. Click the Sources button in the response to open the related links in the side panel and read the sources you need directly. A response without a button means no link was provided, so check it another way. The content, including medical, legal, and financial matters, is not intended to be relied upon as professional advice.

steps.title: Step 4: If the images are mixed
steps.body: If the image to be used in the report may have been created with AI, upload a file to the verification tool to verify. Whether it was created or edited with Google's AI is checked with SynthID, and the source and history are checked with Content Credentials. Because the scope of the two technologies is different, the absence of results does not mean that they are all AI-generated.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: Even within the same app, context determines functionality. If your hands are empty and you are comfortable speaking, use Live, for editing work, use Canvas, for the basis, use the Sources button, and for creation, use the verification tool. If you look at the situation first and choose the function, you won't be confused as to whether Gemini is a search, chatbot, or assistant.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen how to choose a function for each situation, let's summarize the lesson.

screens.title: Theorem: context divides function
screens.lead: Let's summarize what we've seen so far. Read it while thinking about what you want to do with words.

paragraphs: The Gemini app is where you work on ideas, outlines, drafts, and Canvas, and Live is the verbal conversation. Live is available on the Gemini mobile app on your Android phone or tablet, not on the web app. It can interrupt conversations and cannot be used with Gems.

Check the basis for the response with the Sources button. Links may be to public websites, uploaded files, or linked Workspace documents, but not all responses are credited. Having a source doesn't always mean the answer is right, so read where you need to.

Images, videos, and audio created by AI are verified using two technologies: SynthID and Content Credentials. SynthID tells you whether Google's AI model created or edited it, and Content Credentials tells you the origin and history of the content.

Which function is right is determined by the situation, not the name. Ask in that order whether it is easy to talk about, whether there is a result that needs to be corrected, and whether facts need to be confirmed.

Lastly, don’t forget to manage your activities. You can view and delete your conversation history in My Activity, or turn off Keep Activity if you don't want to keep a history. When using Live, which exchanges audio and video, you must also be especially etiquette in asking for permission from others.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: The Gemini app may produce inaccurate or inappropriate responses. Please double-check the responses and do not rely on them as professional advice.

glossary.def: Google's conversational AI app that helps you ideate, outline, draft, and work on Canvas.
Gemini's voice chat feature allows you to communicate verbally and interrupt without input.
This button appears below the response or in the middle of the text and shows related links in a side panel.
This is a watermark that is invisibly placed on AI-created content and is used to determine whether it was created or edited by Google's AI model.
It is a digital passport-like technology that records the source and history of content, and is used for both AI content and non-AI content.

misconceptions.myth: Live can be used in any environment.
misconceptions.fact: Live works with the Gemini mobile app on your Android phone or tablet, but not with the Gemini web app. It also cannot be used with Gems.

misconceptions.myth: Sources are attached to all responses.
misconceptions.fact: Some responses do not provide any relevant links. If there is no Sources button, no link is provided in the response.

misconceptions.myth: Verification tools uncover all AI creations.
misconceptions.fact: SynthID determines the content created or edited by Google's AI models, while Content Credentials informs the source and history of the recording. Each technology has a different range of checks.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: The Gemini app is for drafting, outlining, and Canvas work, and Live is for voice chat.
Check the related sources of the response with the Sources button and read directly where you need to.
Verify AI-generated images, videos, and audio with SynthID and Content Credentials.
The functions used vary depending on the situation.
